memory_update.text: VRT remains a reference anchor for AI data-center thermal and power infrastructure; relationship is evidence-backed, but alpha relevance requires backlog, liquid-cooling revenue, capacity, and valuation checks.
ETN remains a reference anchor for data-center electrical distribution and switchgear demand; official Q1 2026 disclosure supports data-center-driven order/backlog momentum.
MU is a reference HBM supplier for AI accelerator memory stacks; HBM3E/HBM4 transition should be tracked through revenue allocation, qualification, supply commitments, and margin evidence.
TSM is the advanced-packaging/foundry benchmark for the theme; CoWoS/InFO/SoIC capacity disclosures should be used to relay constraints toward substrates, OSATs, test, and tooling candidates.
NVDA is not an underfollowed target but is the architecture anchor: rack-scale liquid cooling, power shelves, busbars, NVLink cabling, and HBM content define downstream supplier research nodes.
AVGO is a reference anchor for custom AI ASICs and Ethernet networking; OpenAI collaboration evidence supports demand mapping for advanced packaging, optics, and networking supply-chain nodes.
ANET is a reference anchor for AI Ethernet networking; use it to monitor scale-up/scale-out Ethernet adoption and related optical-component demand rather than as the primary underfollowed hunt.

FLEX upgraded from Layer-1 hypothesis to evidence-backed underfollowed relationship for AI/cloud data-center power, cooling, rack integration, and infrastructure manufacturing; still needs segment economics and customer validation.

JBL upgraded from Layer-1 hypothesis to evidence-backed underfollowed relationship for AI/cloud data-center EMS, servers, infrastructure, liquid-cooling, and power-management adjacency; still needs revenue/margin/customer validation.
RPI should remain speculative_shadow only: official evidence supports embedded/industrial/OEM computing exposure, not material AI infrastructure supply-chain exposure.
For FLEX and JBL, later layers must verify whether AI infrastructure is material to consolidated revenue and margins rather than merely a product-page or press-release exposure.

For all high-attention reference names, Layer 2C should add market-pricing checks: valuation, expected growth embedded in consensus, analyst coverage, short interest where relevant, and whether bottleneck narratives are already crowded.

This chunk is reference-heavy; the next Serenity pass should deliberately branch from NVDA/TSM/MU/AVGO/ANET/VRT/ETN toward smaller component, tool, test, substrate, cooling, power-module, busbar, CDU, and service suppliers.

summary: Mapped ticker relationships for a mixed reference/underfollowed candidate chunk. Reference leaders validate the AI infrastructure constraint stack: NVDA defines rack-scale GPU architecture, TSM defines leading-edge foundry and advanced-packaging bottlenecks, MU validates HBM as a memory input, AVGO and ANET anchor custom ASIC/Ethernet networking demand, while VRT and ETN anchor data-center thermal and electrical infrastructure. Underfollowed lane candidates FLEX and JBL have stronger-than-Layer-1 evidence after official-source checks: both disclose AI/cloud data-center infrastructure, power/cooling, rack/server, or manufacturing exposure, but still require segment revenue, customer concentration, margin, backlog, and spin-off/acquisition follow-through validation. RPI remains a speculative shadow candidate: official investor materials support embedded/industrial computing exposure, but not material AI data-center infrastructure exposure.
